target_customer: Argentine consumers buying or financing certified used cars
problem: Used-car purchases in Argentina lacked trust and convenience; Checkars sold inspected cars online with paperwork and financing support.
business_model: Online used-car dealer (buy, certify and resell, with financing)

founders.name: Jaime Macaya
founders.background_notes: Left employment in November 2017 to found Checkars per Argentine press

competitors.name: OLX Autos (Frontier Car Group)
competitors.what: Online car buying and selling arm of OLX
competitors.traction_then: arrived in Argentina in September 2019 per press
competitors.funding_then: first investment round of 89 million USD reported

technical_complexity.rationale: Mostly operations: inspection, logistics, paperwork and an e-commerce site; software was standard.

defensibility.rationale: Operations and trust brand helped but a funded rival could replicate the model, as Kavak later did by buying in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Kavak entered Argentina by acquiring Checkars in August 2020 rather than building from scratch.

market_need_then: Press described low trust in used-car transactions and a large Argentine used-car market (Kavak CEO cited roughly 20 billion USD); under 1 percent of used cars sold fully online per a Perfil piece of unclear date.

rebrands.why: Kavak planned co-branding for a few months, then full rebrand by year end per Cronista; later sources still describe Checkars as a Kavak company

brand_strength.rationale: Local press coverage and an NPS above 85 claim, but no source on brand assets; the brand was folded into Kavak within months.

outcome_analysis: Checkars, founded by two former OLX autos executives, reported about 1,500 transactions and 8 million dollars of sales in its first full year and claimed an NPS above 85. In August 2020 Kavak acquired it as its entry to Argentina, committing 10 million dollars, with both founders staying as CEO and COO. The price was not disclosed. It succeeded as a strategic acquisition because a funded regional leader wanted a local team and operation.
notes: Company site returned HTTP 403 on fetch (blocked, not worked around). Seed amount conflicts across outlets: Cronista and Mercado say about 1M USD from private investors (Ureta Saenz Pena, Recchia, Simone named), iProUP says 500K then 750K, Contxto says 1.3M led by Jaguar Ventures, one aggregator says 125K. No consistent date or amount, so no round is recorded. Cronista headline also mentions a 13M USD raise for a later period, unverified. YC lists team size 45 while the shard said otherwise; not used.
